cards.grammarNote:
**점수** = the score (of a game). 점 'point' + 수 'number'.
**몇 점** (myeot jeom) = 'how many points?' is the natural way to ask the score.

**득점** = scoring a point; 득 '득하다 (to gain)' + 점 'point'.
**또** (tto) = 'again', placed before the verb.

**경기** = a match, game, or contest. Very common for all sports events.
**있어요** with a time/place subject = 'there is'.
cards.englishPhrase: There is a soccer match today.

cards.grammarNote:
**토너먼트** = tournament (loanword from English). Also 대회 (daehoe) for broader competitions.
**이기다** = to win; past polite: 이겼어요.

**상대** = opponent, counterpart. Also 상대방 (sangdaebang) in formal contexts.
**이/가 강해요** = '(subject) is strong'; 이/가 after consonant/vowel.

**이기다** = to win (a match or against an opponent). Polite past: 이겼어요.
**을/를** marks the object; 경기를 이겼어요 = 'won the game'.

**지다** = to lose (a game); opposite of 이기다.
**어제** (eoje) = yesterday; time words come before the subject or verb.

**심판** = referee, umpire. Also the act of judging/refereeing.
**호루라기를 불다** = 'to blow the whistle'; 불었어요 is the polite past.

**경기장** = stadium. 경기 'game' + 장 'place'.
**에** after a place = location particle 'in/at'.
cards.englishPhrase: There are many people in the stadium.

cards.grammarNote:
**코치** = coach or trainer (loanword). 감독 (gamdok) is the head manager/director.
**엄격해요** = is strict; 이/가 엄격하다.

**챔피언** = champion (loanword). 세계 챔피언 = world champion.
**이에요/예요** = polite 'is'; use 이에요 after a consonant, 예요 after a vowel.

**팀** = team (loanword). 우리 팀 = our team.
**이겼어요** = won (past polite of 이기다).

**선수** = player, athlete (in competitive sports). 최고의 선수 = 'the best player'.
**최고의** (choego-ui) = 'the best' (possessive).

**무승부** = a tie/draw. 무 'none' + 승부 'win or loss'.
**로 끝났어요** = 'ended in/with …'; 로 marks the result.
cards.englishPhrase: The game ended in a tie.

cards.grammarNote:
**운동선수** = athlete; 운동 'exercise/sport' + 선수 'competitor'.
**이에요** = polite 'is/am/are' after a consonant.

**스포츠** = sport(s) (loanword). Also 운동 (undong) = sports/exercise.
**을/를 좋아해요** = 'like (object)'; 를 after a vowel.

**대회** = competition, contest, event. 激烈한 대회 → 치열한 대회 = intense competition.
**치열해요** = is intense/fierce.

**골을 넣다** = to score a goal; 골 'goal' + 을 넣다 'to put in'.
For points generally use 득점하다 (deukjeom-hada).

**피클볼** = pickleball (loanword). Also written 피클 볼.
**재미있어요** = is fun; literally 'interest exists'.

**패들** = paddle (loanword). 새 패들 = new paddle.
**을 샀어요** = bought (object); 을 after consonant.

**코트** = (sports) court (loanword). 테니스 코트, 배드민턴 코트, etc.
**비어 있어요** = is empty; lit. 'is existing-empty'.

**서브** = serve (loanword); 서브하다 = to serve.
**차례예요** = 'it's (your) turn'; 차례 = turn/order.

**랠리** = a rally / back-and-forth exchange (loanword). 길다 = long.
**긴 랠리** = a long rally.

**공** = ball; also used in compound words: 축구공, 농구공.
**아웃이에요** = 'it's out'; 아웃 = out (bounds).

**네트** = net (loanword for sports net). 인터넷 = the internet.
**에 맞았어요** = 'hit (the net)'; 에 = location particle.

**등산** = hiking/mountain climbing. 등 'to climb' + 산 'mountain'.
**하러 가요** = 'go to do'; 에 가요 = go somewhere.
cards.englishPhrase: We go hiking on the weekend.

cards.grammarNote:
**등산로** = hiking trail/path; 등산 'hiking' + 로 'road/path'.
**좁아요** = is narrow.

**산** = mountain. Korea has many famous mountains (한라산, 설악산).
**높아요** = is high/tall.

**배낭** = backpack; 배낭여행 = backpacking travel.
**이/가 무거워요** = '(subject) is heavy'; 이 after consonant.

**자전거** = bicycle; lit. 'self-propelled cart'. 자전거를 타다 = to ride a bicycle.
**이에요** = is (polite copula after consonant).

**타다** = to ride (vehicles you board: bikes, buses, trains, horses).
**매일** (maeil) = every day; time words come before the verb.
cards.englishPhrase: I ride a bike every day.

cards.grammarNote:
**헬멧** = helmet (loanword). 헬멧을 쓰다 = to put on / wear a helmet.
**쓰세요** = 'please put on/wear' (polite request).

**경주** = a race; 경 'compete' + 주 'run'. Also the city of Gyeongju!
**에서 이겼어요** = 'won (in the race)'; 에서 marks the location of an action.

**야외** = outdoors; 야 'field' + 외 'outside'. 야외 활동 = outdoor activities.
**을/를 좋아해요** = 'like (object)'.

**결승선** = finish line; 결승 'final/decisive' + 선 'line'. Start line = 출발선.
**먼저** = first/before others.
cards.englishPhrase: He reached the finish line first.

cards.grammarNote:
**운동하다** = to exercise/work out; 운동 = exercise/sport.
**매일 아침** = every morning; time phrases precede the verb.

**스트레칭** = stretching (loanword). 스트레칭하다 = to stretch.
**전에** (jeone) = 'before'; V기 전에 = before doing V.

**땀** = sweat; **흘리다** = to shed/drip. Together: to sweat.
**많이** = a lot; placed before the verb.

**훈련** = training; 훈련하다 = to train. Also 트레이닝 (loanword).
**힘들어요** = is tough/hard.

**속도** = speed; 빠르다 = fast (adjective). 속도가 빨라요 = 'the speed is fast'.
**이/가 빨라요** = is fast (subject marker 이 after consonant).

**피곤해요** = I'm tired. Also 지치다 (jichida) = to become exhausted.
**너무** = too/very; placed before the adjective.

**부상** = injury; **입다** = to sustain. Together: to get injured.
**중에** = 'during'; 경기 중에 = during the game.
cards.englishPhrase: He got injured during the game.

cards.grammarNote:
**물** = water; **마시다** = to drink. 물 마시는 거 잊지 마세요 = don't forget to drink water.
**많이** = a lot; **꼭** = definitely/surely.
cards.englishPhrase: Remember to drink lots of water.
cards.phrase: 물을 많이 마시는 거 잊지 마세요.
cards.phraseRomanized: Mureul manhi masineun geo itji maseyo.

cards.grammarNote:
**준비운동** = warm-up exercises; 준비 'preparation' + 운동 'exercise'.
**먼저 … 해요** = 'let's … first'; 먼저 = first.

**코드** = code (loanword). 소스 코드 = source code.
**깔끔해요** = is clean/tidy.

**코딩하다** = to code/program (loanword base). Also 프로그래밍하다.
**밤에** = at night; time expressions come before the verb.
cards.englishPhrase: I like to code at night.

cards.grammarNote:
**소프트웨어** = software (loanword). Hardware = 하드웨어.
**사용하기 쉬워요** = easy to use; 사용하다 = to use.
cards.englishPhrase: This software is easy to use.

cards.grammarNote:
**엔지니어** = engineer (loanword). Also 기술자 (gisulcha).
**소프트웨어 엔지니어** = software engineer.

**개발자** = developer; 개발 'development' + 자 'person'.
**프론트엔드** = front-end (loanword).

**컴퓨터** = computer (loanword). 노트북 = laptop.
**이/가 빨라요** = '(subject) is fast'.

**노트북** = laptop (lit. notebook computer, loanword). Full form: 노트북 컴퓨터.
**가져왔어요** = brought (past polite of 가져오다).

**키보드** = keyboard (loanword). 키 'key' + 보드 'board'.
**사용하기 좋아요** = is nice to use.
cards.englishPhrase: This keyboard is nice to use.

cards.grammarNote:
**화면** = screen/display; 화 'picture' + 면 'surface'. 모니터 is also used.
**너무 밝아요** = too bright; 너무 = too.

**버그** = bug (loanword). Also 오류 (oryu) = error.
**에 있어요** = 'there is in …'; location particle 에.
cards.englishPhrase: There is a bug in the code.

cards.grammarNote:
**디버깅** = debugging (loanword). 디버깅하다 = to debug.
**고 있어요** = progressive (V-고 있어요 = 'is doing V').

**수정하다** = to fix/correct (code). 버그를 수정했어요 = fixed the bug.
**았/었어요** = past tense ending after the verb stem.

**배포하다** = to deploy/release (software). 배포 = deployment/release.
**새 버전** = new version.
cards.englishPhrase: We deploy the new version today.

cards.grammarNote:
**서버** = server (loanword). 서버가 다운됐어요 = the server went down.
**다운됐어요** = went down/crashed.

**데이터베이스** = database (loanword). Often abbreviated 디비 (DB).
**이/가 커요** = is large.

**앱** = app (loanword). Full form: 애플리케이션.
**인기가 많아요** = is popular; lit. 'popularity is much'.

**웹사이트** = website (loanword). 웹 'web' + 사이트 'site'.
**오픈됐어요** = went live/opened (passive past).

**기능** = function/feature of a product. A code function is 함수 (hamsu).
**아직 안 됐어요** = not finished yet; 아직 = still/yet.
cards.phrase: 이 기능은 아직 완성이 안 됐어요.
cards.phraseRomanized: I gineung-eun ajik wanseongi an dwaesseoyo.

cards.grammarNote:
**특성** = characteristic/feature (a property). 기능 is what it does.
**유용해요** = is useful.

**풀 리퀘스트** = pull request (loanword); commonly called PR.
**검토해 주세요** = 'please review'; 주세요 adds politeness.

**회의** = meeting, conference. 회의하다 = to have a meeting.
**이/가 있어요** = 'there is'; 있어요 = exists.
cards.englishPhrase: We have a meeting this afternoon.

cards.grammarNote:
**스탠드업** = standup meeting (loanword). Also 데일리 회의 (daily meeting).
**매일 아침** = every morning.
cards.englishPhrase: There is a standup every morning.

cards.grammarNote:
**마감일** = deadline; 마감 'closing/cutoff' + 일 'day'. Also 데드라인 (loanword).
**이에요** = is (polite copula).

**고객** = client/customer (business). 손님 (sonnim) = guest/customer in everyday service.
**만족해요** = is satisfied.

**재택근무** = work from home; 재택 'at home' + 근무 'work'.
**해요** = do (polite present); 재택근무해요 = 'work from home'.

**원격 근무** = remote work; 원격 'remote/distant' + 근무 'work'.
**은/는** = topic marker; use 는 after a vowel.

**터미널** = terminal (command line; loanword). 커맨드라인 = command line.
**열어요** = open (polite present).

**변수** = variable; 변 'change' + 수 'number'. Constant = 상수 (sangsu).
**정의되지 않았어요** = is not defined.

**저장소** = repository; 저장 'storage' + 소 'place'. Also 레포 (repo, loanword).
**에 있어요** = 'is in …'; 에 = location particle.
cards.englishPhrase: The code is in this repository.

cards.grammarNote:
**브랜치** = branch (git, loanword). Also 가지 (gaji) literally.
**만들었어요** = created (past polite of 만들다).

**검토하다** = to review/examine (code, documents). 점검하다 = general check.
**해 주세요** = 'please do'; adds a polite request.

**테스트** = test(s) (loanword). 테스트하다 = to test.
**다 통과했어요** = all passed; 다 = all.

**업데이트** = update (loanword). 업데이트하다 = to update.
**중요한** = important (adjective before noun).

**심각한** = critical/serious; **오류** = error. 오류 is more technical; 에러 (loanword) is also used.
**발견했어요** = found (past polite of 발견하다).

**프로덕션 환경** = production environment (loanword + 환경 'environment').
**하지 마세요** = 'don't do'; polite negative command.

**팀** = team (loanword). 우리 팀 = our team.
**최고예요** = is the best/great.

**프로젝트** = project (loanword). Also 과제 (gwaje) in academic contexts.
**재미있어요** = is interesting/fun.

**출시하다** = to launch/release (a product). 출시 = product launch.
**다음 주** = next week.
cards.englishPhrase: We launch the product next week.

cards.grammarNote:
**버전** = version (loanword). 최신 버전 = latest version.
**이에요** = is (copula).

**설정하다** = to configure/set up. 설정 = settings/configuration.
**해야 해요** = have to/need to.
cards.englishPhrase: I need to configure the server.

cards.grammarNote:
**환경** = environment (technical or natural). 개발 환경 = dev environment.
**달라요** = is different (polite form of 다르다).
cards.englishPhrase: The dev and prod environments are different.

cards.grammarNote:
**실행하다** = to run/execute (a program). 실행 = execution/running.
**이 프로그램을** = 'this program' (object).

**로그** = log (loanword). 로그를 확인하다 = to check the logs.
**확인해요** = check (polite present).

**푸시하다** = to push (code; loanword). 저장소에 푸시하다 = push to the repository.
**에** = directional/location particle 'to'.
cards.englishPhrase: I pushed the code to the repository.

cards.grammarNote:
**통합** = integration; 통 'unite' + 합 'combine'. 통합 테스트 = integration test.
**실패했어요** = failed (past polite).

**주석** = code comment/annotation. A social comment is 댓글 (daetgeul).
**추가해 주세요** = 'please add'; 추가하다 = to add.

**필요해요** = need; lit. 'it is necessary'. Or 필요가 있어요.
**더 많은** = more; 시간이 더 필요해요 = need more time.

**완료하다** = to complete/finish. 끝내다 (kkeutnaeda) is also common.
**이 작업을** = 'this task (object)'; 작업 = task/work.

**켜다 / 끄다** = to turn on / off.

cards.englishPhrase:
**인터넷** = the internet.
**인터넷을 하다** = to use the internet.

cards.grammarNote: aep
cards.englishPhrase:
**앱** = app; also **어플 / 애플리케이션**.
**깔다** = to install (colloquial for apps).

**카메라** = camera.
**사진을 찍다** = to take a photo.

cards.grammarNote: sajin
cards.phrase: Please take a photo for us.

cards.grammarNote: chungjeonhada
cards.englishPhrase:
**충전하다** = to charge (a device).
**충전 중** = charging (in progress).
cards.phrase: I need to charge my phone.

cards.grammarNote: munja
cards.englishPhrase:
**문자** = text message (lit. 'letters / characters').
**보내다** = to send: *문자를 보내다*.

cards.grammarNote: imeil
cards.phrase: I'll send you an email tomorrow.

cards.grammarNote: kyeoda
cards.englishPhrase:
**켜다** = to turn on (devices / lights).
 Command: **켜 주세요** = please turn (it) on.

cards.grammarNote: kkeuda
cards.englishPhrase:
**끄다** = to turn off; opposite of 켜다.
 Command: **꺼 주세요** = please turn (it) off.

cards.grammarNote: allim
cards.englishPhrase:
**알림** = notification (from 알리다 'to inform').
**끄다 / 켜다** = to turn notifications off / on.

cards.grammarNote: eopdeiteuhada
seuteuriming

**던전** = dungeon (loanword). 어두운 던전 = dark dungeon.
**에 들어갔어요** = 'entered'; 에 = directional particle.

**드래곤** = dragon (loanword). Traditional word: 용 (yong).
**이/가 지키고 있어요** = 'is guarding'; -고 있어요 = progressive.
cards.englishPhrase: A huge dragon guards the treasure.

cards.grammarNote:
**임무** = quest/mission. Also 퀘스트 (loanword from 'quest').
**을/를 받아들였어요** = accepted (object); 받아들이다 = to accept.

**모험** = adventure; 모 'brave' + 험 'danger/险'. 모험하다 = to adventure.
**위험한** = dangerous (adjective before noun).

**캠페인** = campaign (loanword). In D&D, a linked series of sessions.
**계속됐어요** = lasted/continued (past polite).
cards.phrase: 이 캠페인은 몇 달 동안 계속됐어요.
cards.phraseRomanized: I kaempeoin-eun myeot dal dongan gyesoktwaesseoyo.

cards.grammarNote:
**캐릭터** = character/role (loanword). 새 캐릭터 = new character.
**만들었어요** = created.

**마법사** = wizard/mage; 마법 'magic' + 사 'person'. 마법을 쓰다 = to cast a spell.
**화염구** = fireball; 를 던졌어요 = threw/cast (object).

**전사** = warrior/fighter; 전 'battle' + 사 'person'.
**을/를 들어올렸어요** = 'raised (object)'; 들어올리다 = to lift up.

**로그** = rogue (D&D class, loanword). Also 도둑 (doduk) = thief.
**열쇠를 훔쳤어요** = stole the key.

**팔라딘** = paladin (loanword). A holy knight class in D&D.
**용감해요** = is brave.

**레인저** = ranger (loanword). 궁술 = archery.
**을 잘 해요** = 'is good at (object)'; 잘 = well/skillfully.
cards.englishPhrase: The ranger is skilled at archery.

cards.grammarNote:
**던전 마스터** = dungeon master (loanword). Often abbreviated DM.
**장면을 묘사했어요** = described the scene.
cards.englishPhrase: The dungeon master described the scene.

cards.grammarNote:
**주문** = spell (also 'order/incantation'). 마법 주문 = magic spell.
**강력해요** = is powerful.

**주술** = incantation/sorcery; 주 'spell/charm' + 술 'art'. Also 마법 주문.
**외웠어요** = recited (past polite of 외우다).

**마법** = magic; 마 'demon/magic' + 법 'method'. 마법사 = magician.
**가득해요** = is full of.
cards.englishPhrase: The forest is full of magic.

cards.grammarNote:
**포션** = potion (loanword). 마시다 = to drink.
**마세요** = 'please drink' (polite request); 마시다 → 마세요.

**검** = sword (double-edged). A single-edged blade is 칼 (kal).
**날카로워요** = is sharp.

**방패** = shield; 방 'defend' + 패 'plate'.
**로 막으세요** = 'block with'; 로 = instrumental particle.
cards.englishPhrase: Block the attack with your shield.

cards.grammarNote:
**갑옷** = armor; 갑 'shell/plate' + 옷 'clothing'.
**입었어요** = put on/wore (past polite of 입다).

**주사위** = dice/die (native Korean word). 주사위를 굴리다 = to roll the dice.
**위에 있어요** = 'is on top of'; 위에 = on top.
cards.englishPhrase: There are some dice on the table.

cards.grammarNote:
**굴리다** = to roll (a round object). 주사위를 굴리다 = to roll the dice.
**차례예요** = 'it's (your) turn'.
cards.englishPhrase: It's your turn to roll the dice.

cards.grammarNote:
**치명타** = critical hit; 치명 'lethal/decisive' + 타 'strike'.
**이에요** = is (copula).

**레벨업** = level up (loanword). 레벨업하다 = to level up.
**했어요** = did (past polite).

**경험치** = experience points (XP); 경험 'experience' + 치 'value'.
**을/를 얻었어요** = gained (object); 얻다 = to obtain.
cards.englishPhrase: You gained a lot of experience points.

cards.grammarNote:
**몬스터** = monster (loanword). Also 괴물 (goemul) in Korean.
**나타났어요** = appeared (past polite of 나타나다).

**고블린** = goblin (loanword). A small creature from Western fantasy.
**막았어요** = blocked (past polite of 막다).

**보물** = treasure; 보 'precious' + 물 'thing'. 보물을 찾다 = to find treasure.
**찾았어요** = found (past polite).

**지도** = map; 지 'ground' + 도 'diagram'. 지도를 보다 = to look at a map.
**보세요** = 'please look at/see' (polite request).

**선술집** = tavern/pub; 선 'standing' + 술집 'bar'. 여관 (yeogwan) = inn.
**에서 쉬어요** = 'rest at'; 에서 = location of action.

**파티** = party (loanword). 모험 파티 = adventuring party.
**명이에요** = is [number] people; 명 is the counter for people.

**마법이 걸리다** = to have a spell cast on; 걸리다 = to be caught/applied.
**에 마법이 걸려 있어요** = 'is enchanted'; passive state.

**공격하다** = to attack; 공격 = attack/offense.
**빨리** = quickly; placed before the verb.

**도망치다** = to flee/run away; 도망 'escape' + 치다 'dash'.
**기로 했어요** = decided to (V-기로 하다).

**치료하다** = to heal/treat. 성직자 (seongjikja) = cleric/religious person.
**를 치료했어요** = healed (object).

**방어하다** = to defend; 방어 = defense. 공격 = offense.
**해야 해요** = must/have to.

**탐험하다** = to explore; 탐험 = exploration. 탐험가 = explorer.
**같이 … 해요** = 'let's … together'.

**체력** = physical strength/HP; 체 'body' + 력 'power'. Also HP (에이치피).
**이/가 낮아요** = is low.

**턴** = turn (in a game; loanword). Also 차례 (charye) = turn/order.
**내 턴이에요** = 'it's my turn'.

**승리** = victory; 승 'win' + 리 '利 benefit/victory'. 승리하다 = to triumph.
**결국** = in the end/finally.
cards.englishPhrase: In the end we achieved victory.

cards.grammarNote:
**적** = enemy, foe. Also 적군 (jeokgun) = enemy troops.
**점점 가까워지고 있어요** = getting closer and closer; 점점 = gradually.

**함정** = trap/pitfall; 함 'pit' + 정 'well'. Also 덫 (deot) = a snare trap.
**조심하세요** = be careful (polite).

**전리품** = loot/spoils; 전 'battle' + 리품 'prize goods'.
**을/를 나눴어요** = split/divided (object); 나누다 = to divide.

**여관 주인** = innkeeper; 여관 'inn' + 주인 'owner'.
**소식** = news/information; 소식을 전해줬어요 = gave us news.
cards.englishPhrase: The innkeeper gave us some news.

cards.grammarNote:
**활** = bow (weapon); an arrow is 화살 (hwasal).
**로 맞혔어요** = 'hit with'; 로 = instrumental particle.
cards.englishPhrase: She hit the target with her bow.

cards.grammarNote:
**게임 세션** = game session (loanword). Also 판 (pan) = a round/session.
**이 있어요** = 'there is a'; existence expression.

**규칙** = rule(s); 규 'rule' + 칙 'standard'. 규칙을 지키다 = to follow/keep rules.
**지켜 주세요** = 'please follow'; 주세요 adds polite request.

**선제권** = initiative; 선제 'preemptive' + 권 'right'. Also 이니셔티브 (loanword).
**순서를 정해요** = determine the order.

**이십면체** = icosahedron/twenty-sided; 이십 'twenty' + 면 'face' + 체 'body'.
**을 사용하세요** = 'please use (object)'.
cards.englishPhrase: Use the d20 for the check.

cards.grammarNote:
**설날** = Korean Lunar New Year, the biggest traditional holiday. Families gather for ancestral rites.
**가장 중요한** = the most important (superlative).
cards.englishPhrase: Seollal is the most important Korean holiday.

cards.grammarNote:
**추석** = Chuseok, Korea's harvest moon festival. Families visit ancestral hometowns and eat songpyeon.
**에** = at/on (time particle).

**한복** = traditional Korean clothing worn at holidays and ceremonies.
**을 입다** = to wear (clothing); 입어요 = polite present.

**세배** = the formal deep bow given to elders on Seollal. Children receive 세뱃돈 (pocket money) in return.
**드려요** = give (humble form of 주다, used toward elders).
cards.englishPhrase: Children give their elders a sebae bow.

cards.grammarNote:
**김치** = fermented spiced vegetables, a staple side dish at every Korean meal.
**이/가 맵지만** = 'is spicy but'; 지만 = contrast connector.

**반찬** = small side dishes served alongside rice at a Korean meal. Many are shared communally.
**여러 가지** = various kinds.
cards.englishPhrase: A Korean meal has various side dishes.
cards.phrase: 한국 식사에는 반찬이 여러 가지 있어요.
cards.phraseRomanized: Hanguk siksa-eneun banchan-i yeoleo gaji isseoyo.

cards.grammarNote:
**존댓말** = formal/honorific speech; 반말 (banmal) = casual speech. Choosing correctly shows respect.
**써야 해요** = should use (V-아/어야 하다 = must/should).
cards.englishPhrase: You should use honorifics with elders.

cards.grammarNote:
**찜질방** = a public Korean sauna/spa facility; families spend the night, eat eggs, and rest.
**에서 쉬어요** = rest at (location of action).
cards.englishPhrase: Korean families often rest at the jjimjilbang.

cards.grammarNote:
**노래방** = private karaoke room; 노래 'song' + 방 'room'. Popular for all ages.
**에 가요** = go to (destination particle 에).
cards.englishPhrase: Let's go to the norebang after dinner.

cards.grammarNote:
**빨리빨리** = 'hurry up!' or 'quickly quickly' — Korea's culture of urgency and efficiency.
**문화** = culture; 빨리빨리 문화 = the bbali-bbali culture.

**봄** = spring. Korean springs are famous for cherry blossoms (벚꽃).
**에는** = in (season/time topic); 봄에는 = 'in spring'.

**여름** = summer. Korean summers are hot and humid with a monsoon season (장마철).
**이/가 더워요** = is hot.
cards.englishPhrase: Korean summer is hot and humid.

cards.grammarNote:
**가을** = autumn/fall. Known for beautiful foliage and the harvest festival (추석).
**단풍이 들어요** = the leaves turn (colors); 단풍 = autumn leaves.
cards.englishPhrase: In autumn the leaves turn beautiful colors.

cards.grammarNote:
**겨울** = winter. Koreans enjoy skiing and hot foods like 떡볶이 and 어묵 in winter.
**이/가 추워요** = is cold.
cards.englishPhrase: Korean winters are cold and dry.

cards.grammarNote:
**떡볶이** = spicy stir-fried rice cakes, a very popular Korean street food snack.
**인기가 많아요** = is popular; lit. 'popularity is much'.
cards.englishPhrase: Tteokbokki is a popular Korean street food.
cards.phrase: 떡볶이는 인기 있는 한국 길거리 음식이에요.
cards.phraseRomanized: Tteokbokki-neun ingi inneun hanguk gilgeori eumsig-ieyo.

cards.grammarNote:
**불고기** = thinly sliced marinated beef, grilled at the table; 불 'fire' + 고기 'meat'.
**유명해요** = is famous.
cards.englishPhrase: Bulgogi is a famous Korean dish.

cards.grammarNote:
**피부 관리** = skincare; 피부 'skin' + 관리 'management'. Korean skincare (K-뷰티) is globally famous.
**이/가 유명해요** = is famous.
cards.phrase: 한국 피부 관리는 전 세계적으로 유명해요.
cards.phraseRomanized: Hanguk pibu gwanri-neun jeon seagyejeogeur-o yumyeonghaeyo.

cards.grammarNote:
**케이팝** = K-pop (Korean popular music, loanword). Also written K-팝.
**전 세계적으로** = worldwide; 에서 인기가 있어요 = 'is popular'.
cards.englishPhrase: K-pop is popular all over the world.

cards.grammarNote:
**나이** = age; Korean culture places great importance on age hierarchy, affecting speech levels and social roles.
**중요해요** = is important.
cards.englishPhrase: In Korea, age is very important in social relationships.

cards.grammarNote:
**소주** = soju, a clear distilled spirit — Korea's most popular alcoholic drink.
**마셔요** = drink (polite present of 마시다).
cards.englishPhrase: Soju is Korea's most popular alcoholic drink.
cards.phrase: 소주는 한국에서 가장 인기 있는 술이에요.
cards.phraseRomanized: Soju-neun hanguk-eseo gajang ingi inneun sul-ieyo.

cards.grammarNote:
**같이 먹기** = eating together from shared dishes, a core part of Korean dining etiquette.
**문화예요** = 'is a culture/custom'.
cards.englishPhrase: Sharing dishes is an important part of Korean dining.
cards.phrase: 음식을 같이 먹는 건 한국 식사 문화예요.
cards.phraseRomanized: Eumsig-eul gachi meogneun geon hanguk siksa munhwayeyo.

cards.grammarNote:
**돌잔치** = a big celebration for a baby's first birthday; 돌 = first anniversary + 잔치 = feast.
**을 열어요** = hold (an event); 열다 = to open/hold.
cards.englishPhrase: Families hold a big doljanchi for a baby's first birthday.
cards.phrase: 아기의 첫 번째 생일에 돌잔치를 열어요.
cards.phraseRomanized: Agi-ui cheot beonjjae saengil-e doljanchi-reul yeoleoyo.

cards.grammarNote:
**제사** = ancestral memorial rites, held on death anniversaries and major holidays like Chuseok.
**를 지내요** = hold/perform (a ritual).
cards.englishPhrase: Korean families perform ancestral rites on Chuseok.

cards.grammarNote:
**고추장** = fermented red pepper paste, a staple in Korean cooking; 고추 'chili' + 장 'paste'.
**에 들어가요** = goes into / is used in.
cards.englishPhrase: Gochujang is used in many Korean dishes.

cards.grammarNote:
**한류** = the Korean Wave; the global spread of Korean pop culture (K-pop, K-drama, food, etc.).
**전 세계로** = to all over the world; 퍼지고 있어요 = is spreading (progressive).
cards.englishPhrase: The Korean Wave has spread around the world.

cards.grammarNote:
**무당** = shaman (traditional Korean folk religion). Shamanistic rituals (굿) still exist today.
**전통 종교예요** = is a traditional religion.
cards.englishPhrase: Shamanism is part of Korea's traditional spiritual heritage.
cards.phrase: 무당 신앙은 한국의 전통 민간 신앙이에요.
cards.phraseRomanized: Mudang sinang-eun hanguk-ui jeontong mingan sinang-ieyo.

cards.grammarNote:
**교육열** = passion for education; 교육 'education' + 열 'enthusiasm/fever'. Korea is famous for its intensive education culture, including 학원 (private academies).
**높아요** = is high.
cards.englishPhrase: Korea has a strong passion for education.
